id.description: Board project id: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, unique, not _board. It names the project on its tasks, in the journal and in its source ids such as jira:<id> and github:<id>:<repo>.

type.description: jira: tasks come from the Jira issues jql returns, read with JIRA_EMAIL and JIRA_API_TOKEN from secrets.env.

baseUrl.description: Jira site URL. https:, or http: only on a loopback host.

jql.description: Jira search whose issues become tasks in To Do. A task whose issue leaves the result is flagged out of filter while it has an open PR or a live session, and is archived otherwise, once Spur, the tracker and every repo have a complete poll since its last change and none of them is blind; a task added or removed by hand is left alone.

items.description: A Jira status name, spelled exactly as in Jira.

doneStatuses.description: Jira statuses that mean done. A task whose issue is in one of them and that has no open PR is archived on the next archive.doneWeekday, once every repo has a complete poll since its last change. Each name must exist in every projectKeys project, or the Jira poll fails with a config error.

items.description: A Jira status name, spelled exactly as in Jira.

readyStatuses.description: Jira statuses that mean ready for development. The board checks only that each name exists in every projectKeys project; the Jira poll fails with a config error otherwise.

projectKeys.description: Keys of this board project's Jira projects, such as PROJ. A PR names its task by one of these keys, and doneStatuses and readyStatuses are checked in each of these projects. A task key such as PROJ-12 belongs to the one board project whose list holds its prefix; an empty list takes every Jira key, and a key that several projects take belongs to none. The Jira poll fails with a config error while the list is empty.

items.description: A Jira project key in capitals, such as PROJ.

type.description: github-issues: tasks come from the open issues of tracker.repo, narrowed by label or milestone when set, read with GITHUB_TOKEN.

repo.description: Repository as owner/name whose open issues become tasks. PRs link to its issues only in this repository, so list it in repos too.

label.description: Only open issues with this label become tasks. Set at most one of label and milestone; with neither, every open issue of tracker.repo becomes a task.

milestone.description: Only open issues in the milestone with this title become tasks. Set at most one of label and milestone; with neither, every open issue of tracker.repo becomes a task.

repos.description: GitHub repositories as owner/name whose PRs the board polls for this project, one source each. A done task is archived only after every listed repository has a complete poll since its last change.

reposWithoutCi.description: Repos from repos that run no CI checks, in any letter case. In a listed repo, a PR whose check list on head is empty passes the Dev gate check condition instead of waiting in Dev. A list of only skipped checks still waits, and red or pending checks still count. A listed repo whose branch protection requires checks that have not reported yet also passes, so list only repos that run no checks. Without this key, a PR with no checks waits in Dev.

items.description: A repository from repos as owner/name, in any letter case.

checksGate.description: The column whose exit requires green checks on the PR head: dev (the default), review, product-review or external-review, and the column must be enabled. Running checks, or no checks yet, hold a task only at the exit of this column. Red checks return the task to Dev from any column; a task whose turn is taken returns right after that turn's submit. A task enters ready-to-merge only with green checks. With dev, a cancelled check is red at once. With another column, a cancelled check counts as running until two complete GitHub polls after the one that saw it, about two GitHub poll intervals, and then counts as red; a new run in that window replaces it, and a source whose polls stay incomplete keeps it running. The daemon reads the key at start, so a change takes effect after a restart.

approvalWatch.description: Top-level directories and root files whose change after an approval the board points out. For each approval of an open PR given on an older commit than the head, board status and board task list every top-level entry changed by the commits after it in changedAfter, and the entries that match this list in watchedAfter. Without the key every changed top-level entry counts as watched. A hint only: no gate, move or turn reads it. The daemon reads the key at start, so a change takes effect after a restart.

items.description: One top-level directory (back/) or root file (package.json) of the repository. The trailing / is optional: back/ and back each match a directory or a file named back. Case-sensitive.

link.description: How a project links a PR to its task. A github-issues project reads an issue number from PRs in tracker.repo; a Jira project reads an issue key with one of tracker.projectKeys from PRs in repos. Left at the defaults, a Jira project links every tracker.projectKeys key (such as PROJ-12, any letter case) in the PR title or head branch. Set the sources and patterns to the branch and PR title naming rules of the repos. The board does not enforce those rules; the repo enforces them through its CI title check and its agents' skills. board doctor compares these rules with recent PRs by operatorGithubLogin.

sources.description: Where a PR names its task, in priority order; the first source that yields an issue number wins (for a Jira project, an issue key). closing: issues in tracker.repo the PR closes (Closes #12 in the body, or linked in the sidebar), for PRs to the default branch only; a Jira project skips it. branch: branchPattern on the head branch. title: titlePattern on the PR title.

items.description: One place a PR can name its task: closing, branch or title.

branchPattern.description: Regular expression that starts with ^ and whose one capture group reads the issue number from a PR head branch, such as <agent>-<number>-<slug>. Branches longer than 255 characters are not matched. For a Jira project the capture group reads the issue key, such as PROJ-12, which must use one of tracker.projectKeys in any letter case; left at the default, a Jira project finds every such key in the PR head branch.

titlePattern.description: Regular expression that starts with ^ and whose one capture group reads the issue number from a PR title, such as fix(core): #12 summary. Titles longer than 255 characters are not matched. For a Jira project the capture group reads the issue key, such as PROJ-12, which must use one of tracker.projectKeys in any letter case; left at the default, a Jira project finds every such key in the PR title.

operatorGithubLogin.description: The GitHub account agents open PRs under. PR discovery in repos keeps only PRs whose author is this login. It is not necessarily the maintainer's own account: when agents push as one account and a maintainer approves as another, set the agents' account, or no PR is discovered. Comments, reviews and approvals by this login or by a bot (GitHub App) are not external: they never return a task to Dev, approve External Review or block its approval. Every other account is external, the repo owner's and the human operator's included.

spurProjects.description: Spur projects whose sessions work on this board project, each with a role; at most one curator. An operator listed here replaces the top-level spurProjects operator for this project. Board commands from a session whose Spur project is in no spurProjects list, here or top-level, are refused.

name.description: The name of the project in Spur. A Spur project can be listed under only one board project.

role.description: worker: sessions of this Spur project may link to this project's tasks through their PR or branch. operator: sessions act as the operator of this board project only. orchestrator: sessions execute named columns and never become task workers. curator: sessions answer the questions no column orchestrator takes and escalate the rest to the operator; a board project has at most one.

shortName.description: The name the operator types as @<shortName> at the start of a new message in the orchestrators channel to start a conversation with this Spur project's live session. Unique across the board.

displayName.description: The name Slack messages this Spur project's sessions write are posted under: block threads and replies, and a curator's answer lines in the feed. Defaults to the Spur project name.

icon.description: The emoji shortcode, such as :owl:, shown on those messages instead of the role icon.

columns.description: The project's board columns in canonical order. todo, dev and done must be present and enabled. A column left out or disabled is skipped. Without this key, every built-in column is enabled with orchestrator none except triage, listed disabled. todo, triage and ready-for-dev form the Todo group: the dispatcher never moves a task between them.

id.description: The built-in column this entry configures.

enabled.description: false skips the column: tasks move past it and its exit condition is not checked. todo, dev and done cannot be disabled.

orchestrator.description: Who takes the column's turns. none: the task's live worker session, else the operator. operator: the operator, who also gets the questions asked in the column. Otherwise the name of a spurProjects entry with role orchestrator or curator whose sessions orchestrate the column and get the questions others ask in it. A column left at none, and enabled, takes the top-level spurProjects orchestrator that lists it.

cycleLimit.description: How many times a task may return to Dev from this column before the board stops it for the operator. Returns by the column executor, for external comments and for unresolved review threads count, a changes-requested review included (it is an external comment, not a separate return); a conflict, red CI and a draft do not.

courseCheck.description: How many returns to Dev from this column, counted as for cycleLimit, before the board holds the task and asks courseCheckTo (by default the curator, or the operator when the project has no curator) to check its course. The answer resets the count and reaches the worker as a task comment. 0 turns the check off; cycleLimit is checked first. With External Review enabled, returns for external comments from any column, and each external change request on a new PR head while the task is in Dev (once per head), count toward External Review's courseCheck instead of this column's; cycleLimit still counts them per column.

courseCheckTo.description: Who answers this column's course check: operator, the curator's name, or the name of a column orchestrator listed in this project's spurProjects; a board-wide orchestrator is refused. Without it, the curator, or the operator when the project has no curator. When the addressee has no live session the question moves to the operator; a conductor that is rung and does not answer keeps it, and the operator gets an item.

requireResolvedThreads.description: true: a task leaves this column, and every column right of it, only when its PR has no unresolved review thread; an unresolved one sends it back to Dev, and the worker's Dev turn lists each thread. Outdated threads count; a thread counts until someone resolves it, whoever wrote it. Defaults to true on ready-to-merge and false elsewhere; allowed on dev through ready-to-merge.

approvalRule.description: What lets a task leave External Review. any-approval, the default: an approval by someone other than operatorGithubLogin and no changes requested by one. github-rules: that, and GitHub's review rule for the PR's base branch, from branch protection and rulesets, met on the PR's head: no changes requested (GitHub's review decision counts only once the merge state is computed), a required check completed, or, when none is required, every check except skipped ones green and at least one (no checks at all also counts); and the merge not blocked. A required check, one GitHub marks required or a context the rule lists, pending or without a run GitHub marks required holds the head on CI unless the merge state is clean, unstable or has hooks. Only on the external-review column; a disabled one ignores it.

quietAfterMs.description: How long a task may wait in External Review with an open PR and no new external review round before the board raises one operator item (external-quiet:) for it, in milliseconds. The wait runs from the latest of the task entering the column, the last Dev submit or arrival of the current PR head, and the last external review on the PR. While the PR source is blind or stale no item is raised and a raised one stays; that time still counts. A new external review, a new head or leaving the column clears the item. A signal only: it moves nothing and opens no turn. 0 or unset turns it off; else at least 300000 (5 minutes). Only on the external-review column; a disabled one ignores it.

quietTurnAfterMs.description: How long the orchestrator session holding a turn of this column may sit quiet at its prompt before the board reminds it, then raises a stuck-turn anomaly, in milliseconds. Defaults to health.idleInDevAfterMs. Named orchestrator only: allowed on an enabled column whose orchestrator is a Spur project, set here or filled board-wide; a worker or operator turn left in the column keeps health.idleInDevAfterMs.

noRecipientAfterMs.description: How long an untaken turn of this column may wait with no live session to ring before the board raises one operator item for the project and column, in milliseconds. The time runs from the later of the turn ring's creation and the moment the last session that could take it stopped being a recipient: the first of its end, leaving Spur's list or reaching a finished state (stopped, killed, errored or completed), so later changes in the same gap do not move it. Sessions that could take it are those of the column's Spur project and the task's linked orchestrator. Defaults to 600000 (10 minutes). Named orchestrator only: allowed on an enabled column whose orchestrator is a Spur project, set here or filled board-wide.

source.description: Where ready-for-dev takes its tasks from: manual (the default), or a GitHub Project field mirrored by the board. Only on the ready-for-dev column.

anyOf.description: manual: the operator moves tasks into and out of the column, the default.

type.description: tracker: the board places idle Todo-group tasks between todo and ready-for-dev from the status of their issue in a GitHub Project, read on every poll with GITHUB_TOKEN (scope read:project). An issue whose field has the value moves to ready-for-dev; one that loses it, leaves the Project or is archived there moves back to todo. Tasks with started work, and triage, are never moved. Manual moves into or out of ready-for-dev are refused with column_mirrored. A failed or incomplete read moves nothing. Only on the ready-for-dev column of a github-issues project.

project.description: The GitHub Project as owner/number: the user or organization login that owns it and its number from the Project URL.

field.description: Name of the single-select field of the Project to read, such as Status.

value.description: The option of field that places a task in ready-for-dev, such as Ready; matched to an option name exactly, letter case included.

dispatcher.description: How the board moves tasks between columns. The board records the mode it last ran with. The daemon reads the mode at start, so a change takes effect after a restart; a switch from shadow to on copies the shadow column of each task into its column, and a switch back to shadow closes the open turns and starts the shadow column from the column again.

mode.description: shadow: the board evaluates the column gates and records where each task would go in its shadow column, and opens no turn, doorbell or block; the column executor submits with the task key. on: the board moves the task between columns, hands the column executor a turn, and raises the cycle-limit and course-check blocks.

submitConfirmMs.description: How long the board waits to confirm a turn submit it accepted pending (no PR linked yet, or GitHub not confirming the head) before handing the turn back to its executor with the reason in milliseconds.

projects.description: Board projects, at least one. Each reads tasks from one tracker and PRs from its repos. A Spur project can be listed under only one board project; one that serves several goes in top-level spurProjects.

spurProjects.description: Spur projects bound board-wide, each with role orchestrator or operator. A project-level binding wins for its own project. A Spur project here serves every board project it binds, and one of its sessions acts on the turns, inbox, questions and doorbells of each of them and no other.

name.description: The name of the project in Spur. It must not also be listed under any projects[].spurProjects, and none and operator are reserved.

role.description: orchestrator: sessions execute the listed columns in every board project that enables the column and leaves its orchestrator at none. operator: sessions act as the operator of every board project that lists no operator of its own; a project's own operator acts only in its project. At most one operator.

columns.description: Required for role orchestrator, not allowed for operator. The columns it executes board-wide. A project column whose orchestrator is set to anything but none keeps it, and a disabled column is never filled; it must fill at least one column in some board project.

items.description: A built-in column this orchestrator executes.

shortName.description: The name the operator types as @<shortName> at the start of a new message in the orchestrators channel to start a conversation with this Spur project's live session. Unique across the board, top-level and projects[].spurProjects alike.

displayName.description: The name Slack messages this Spur project's sessions write are posted under. Defaults to the Spur project name.

icon.description: The emoji shortcode, such as :owl:, shown on those messages instead of the role icon.

slack.description: Slack user ID of the operator, such as U0123456789. Slack commands, button presses and messages from anyone else are denied. A feed line the operator resolves names this user.

appName.description: Slack app and bot display name that board slack manifest writes when --app-name is not given.

command.description: Slash command with its leading slash. The board acts only on this command, and board slack manifest writes it when --command is not given. When slack.channels is set and SLACK_APP_CONFIG_TOKEN and slack.appId are present, board doctor compares it with the installed app.

appId.description: Slack app ID, such as A0123456789. When slack.channels is set and SLACK_APP_CONFIG_TOKEN is present, board doctor reads this app's manifest to check the installed slash command against slack.command.

orchestrators.description: Slack channel ID, such as C0123456789, where the board opens a thread for each block addressed to the operator by someone else. Once either channel is set, the daemon does not start without the other channel and SLACK_BOT_TOKEN, and without SLACK_APP_TOKEN it reads nothing from Slack.

feed.description: Slack channel ID where the board posts a line for each curator answer, each newly installed version, each revoked operator token, each `/board tokens` list and each operator item, with the buttons the operator presses. Operator items about failed Slack posts, transport health and undelivered answers, and those shown as operator blocks, get no feed line. A line whose item clears before it is first sent, such as an expired token request, is dropped. Set it together with orchestrators.

defaultAddressee.description: The shortName, top-level or under projects[].spurProjects, of the Spur project that gets a new orchestrators-channel message which does not start with a known @<shortName>. Without it, such a message goes to the top-level spurProjects operator; without one, when any shortName is set, to the operator of the first board project that lists one; otherwise it gets one reply listing the valid prefixes, or is skipped when no shortName is configured.

staleMultiplier.description: A source with no complete poll for this many of its poll intervals turns blind stale. board status marks that source, and an operator item whose fact is older than that, as stale.

blockOpenMs.description: How long a block may stay open before an item is raised in milliseconds.

doneWeekday.description: Weekday whose local midnight, in digest.tz, is the weekly archive slot: tasks done before it are archived then, once their repos have a complete poll since their last change. A slot missed while the daemon was down is applied on the next tick.

tz.description: IANA time zone, such as Europe/Berlin, for the archive.doneWeekday slot and the times shown in resolved feed lines.

retentionDays.description: Days the board keeps each caller's mutation --key with its input and result. In that time the same caller and key with the same input returns the stored result, and with a different input the call is refused. A daily job deletes older keys.

unusedAfterDays.description: Days an approved operator access key from board token create may go unused before board doctor warns about it.

firstRetryMs.description: Wait after the first unanswered doorbell in milliseconds.

secondRetryMs.description: Wait after the second unanswered doorbell in milliseconds.

unansweredAfterMs.description: Wait after the third unanswered doorbell in milliseconds.

port.description: Local HTTP API port (0 assigns a free port). The default 4777 is above 4310-4399, a margin kept for Spur's server port 4310 and the ports from 4311 upward that its MCP port takes, and avoids Spur's ports 5555 and 8730-8799 and the Linux ephemeral range 32768-60999.
Optional web listener port (0 assigns a free port); omitted means off. Set together with publicOrigin. Must differ from http.port, including when both are 0.

publicOrigin.description: Bare public HTTP/HTTPS origin for the web API; HTTP requires loopback. Set together with port. Every {port} is replaced with the listener port, including in hostnames. No trailing slash. The resolved origin must remain valid and HTTP loopback-only after actual-port substitution; the resolver returns no origin for an invalid actual port or resulting origin.

spurUiOrigin.description: Optional concrete bare origin for the Spur UI, independently of the web API. HTTP works on any host without voice; no placeholders or trailing slash. Unset or unreachable UI only warns in doctor and never blocks updates.

portRange.description: Optional stand port range, effectively 4780..4799 when omitted. An explicit range (including {}) must exclude http.port and web.port; an omitted range preserves legacy configs and doctor warns on overlaps. pnpm stand takes its web port, and an explicit API port, from this range and refuses http.port and web.port.

min.description: Inclusive first stand port; defaults to 4780 when a range is supplied.

max.description: Inclusive last stand port; defaults to 4799 when a range is supplied.

intervalMs.description: Time between two polls in milliseconds.

baseUrl.description: Base URL of the local Spur HTTP API.

intervalMs.description: Time between two polls in milliseconds.
Time between two polls in milliseconds.
Time between two polls in milliseconds.

authRetryMs.description: Wait before polling a source again after an auth error in milliseconds.

goneAfterPolls.description: Complete polls an entity must be missing from before it counts as gone.

reserveRemaining.description: GitHub API requests to leave unused in each quota window.

turnStallAfterMs.description: How long an unhealthy open-turn executor waits before a curator or operator block in milliseconds.

errorAfterMs.description: How long a session stays in error before it is flagged in milliseconds.

needsInputAfterMs.description: How long a session waits for input before it is flagged in milliseconds.

idleInDevAfterMs.description: How long a worker session without an open PR, or the executor of a taken turn, waits at its prompt before it is flagged; an orchestrator turn uses its column quietTurnAfterMs when set in milliseconds.

flipSmoothingMs.description: How long a new session health value must hold before it is reported in milliseconds.

sessions.description: Sessions entering error within the window that start an episode.

windowMs.description: Window in which that many sessions entering error start a host-load episode in milliseconds.

maxEpisodeMs.description: Longest a host-load episode lasts before error flags resume in milliseconds.
